# US-07.1 — Choose a city, temperature and image and run an analysis

| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Epic**         | [EPIC-07 Interactive Dashboard & Heat Visualizer](../epics/EPIC-07-dashboard.md) |
| **Priority**     | P1                                                                               |
| **Estimate**     | 3                                                                                |

| **Files**        | `frontend/app.py`, `frontend/.streamlit/config.toml`                             |

## User story

**As an** analyst,
**I want** to select a city, ambient temperature and aerial image before running an analysis,
**so that** I can inspect a chosen urban zone under the simulated conditions.

Traceability: **STORY-017 → EPIC-007 → FR-22** in [requirements](../../../agile/requirements.md); NFR-2, NFR-5 and NFR-8 also apply.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Dashboard shell**
Given the dashboard starts,
when the page renders,
then it is titled HotSpot Sentinels, uses a wide layout and the configured dark theme, and shows the controls without a startup error.

**AC2 — City and temperature**
Given the sidebar,
when I select Singapore, Bangkok or Delhi and adjust the slider,
then the selection carries that city's coordinate defaults and accepts 30.0–45.0 °C in 0.5 °C steps with an initial value of 36.5 °C.

**AC3 — Preset or upload**
Given locally seeded presets or a supported custom image,
when I select the input,
then the selected aerial image is previewed and is the image submitted on Run Analysis.

**AC4 — Configured API request**
Given `API_BASE_URL` is configured or unset,
when I run an analysis,
then a multipart request sends the image with its actual MIME type, selected temperature and selected city identity/coordinates to the configured `/api/analyze` endpoint, defaulting to `http://localhost:8080` without a deployed URL literal.

## Tasks

- [x] Call `st.set_page_config` before other Streamlit calls with the correct title and wide layout
- [x] Provide a custom JPEG/PNG uploader, image preview and analysis button
- [ ] Apply the dark theme through `frontend/.streamlit/config.toml` rather than CSS alone
- [ ] Add the three-city selector and its coordinate defaults
- [ ] Correct the slider bounds/default and actually submit its value
- [ ] Add locally seeded preset selection with cached image loading and support the API's accepted PNG, JPEG and WebP formats
- [ ] Read `API_BASE_URL` from the environment for both analysis and scan history
- [ ] Preserve the real uploaded MIME type and use the accepted EPIC-05 multipart contract
- [ ] Keep all scoring, unit conversion and cloud access outside the UI

## Current state

The 128-line [dashboard](../../../frontend/app.py) has a wide page, custom dark CSS, JPEG/PNG upload, image preview, a Run HotSpot Analysis button and an analysis spinner. There is no theme configuration file, city selector or preset picker. The slider is 25.0–45.0 °C with default 35.0 °C; `simulated_temp` is never submitted. The POST sends only `file`, labels every upload `image/jpeg`, and hardcodes a deployed Cloud Run URL; scan history hardcodes the same service.

The UI makes no direct cloud calls, but a valid current report cannot fill every displayed field: it still reads deleted `surface_temp_estimate_c` and `requires_emergency_alert`. STORY-018 and STORY-020 capture the rendering defects; the orchestrator must file them. Analysis submission remains blocked by EPIC-05's unfinished request contract, including BUG-007, and slider/MIME/URL defects also need orchestrator triage rather than silent backlog writes here.

## Test cases

| Test                                                | Asserts                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_dashboard_shell_is_dark_and_wide`             | Startup renders the expected title, layout and configured theme                              |
| `test_city_and_temperature_controls`                | All three cities and the exact metric slider bounds, step and default are available          |
| `test_selected_image_is_previewed_and_submitted`    | Preset/custom image preview matches submitted bytes                                          |
| `test_dashboard_posts_configured_multipart_request` | Mocked POST targets the env-selected endpoint with correct MIME, temperature and city fields |

Use Streamlit AppTest with mocked HTTP; no live backend or cloud credentials belong in pytest.

## Definition of done

All four criteria pass with mocked HTTP and the accepted API contract, the page follows the [dashboard instructions](../../instructions/streamlit-ui.instructions.md), and the offline suite stays green without coverage regression.
